title: Latency fire drill — weekly perf sync notes (Dec 12 2024)
content:
Attendees: Asha (notes), Marco, Sofia, Diego, Priya
Date: 2024-12-12 weekly perf sync — ad-hoc "fire-drill" after multiple customer reports of higher p95 on medium-length chat workloads.
Context / TL;DR:
- We saw a reproducible regression in p95 latency for 4k-token-ish chat sessions starting around 2024-12-10 (deploy window).
- Regression surface: p95 up ~70–80ms -> ~200ms (hosted clusters, A100 80GB pools), p99 spikes to 1.1–1.3s under load; throughput (stable RPS) dropped ~18% for the same GPU pool configuration.
- Immediate impact: two mid-market customers reported slower bot responses; we triggered enhanced logging and a canary rollback in one region.

Recent runs (summary):
- Run ID: nightly-bench-2024-12-11-03 (canary env, 8xA100-80GB)
  - Model: openchat-13b-8k (float16 baseline)
  - Seq dist: median 512, 90th 2048, 99th 4096 tokens
  - Batch size: 4 continuous-batching config (max-latency-slo=250ms)
  - Result: p50 42ms, p95 198ms (baseline typically ~120ms), p99 1187ms, throughput 420 RPS (baseline 512 RPS)

- Run ID: perf-smoke-2024-12-12-08 (devbox, single A100)
  - Experiment: revert PR 1423 build + run with prior kernel
  - Result: p95 125ms, p99 260ms, throughput 498 RPS -> suggests change in PR 1423 correlated with regression.

Hypothesis / immediate suspects:
1) PR #1423 (kernel selection refactor) changed a loop ordering for attention kernels; microbenchmarks OK but integration may degrade batching behavior for mid-long sequences.
2) Batcher config change: a new greedy timeout of 12ms was introduced in a landing PR on 2024-12-09 and could cause smaller effective batches under observed seq distributions.
3) cudnn/cuBLAS driver upgrade in the infra image (2024-12-10) — larger step-change for some fused kernels.
4) KV-cache warmup behavior: additional memcpy observed at cold start for ~50ms in traces.

Evidence gathered during sync:
- Flamegraphs from grafana trace (linked) show increased time in a function named attention_v2::apply_gemm for the slow runs.
- Logs: metric 'batch_size_effective' on the canary cluster dropped from 3.8 -> 2.1 at peak.
- Reverting PR 1423 in a dev run restored ~90% of baseline throughput.

Notes from people:
- Marco: microbenchmarks on attention kernels show 5–8% regression for multi-head sizes with padded sequence lengths. Suspects loop unrolling assumptions.
- Sofia: Batcher telemetry indicates timeout changes were applied in staging; will roll back the timeout and re-run canary. Ticket INF-3150 opened.
- Diego: infra image pinned cudnn to previous working version in a test cluster; early results match partial recovery.
- Priya: customer-facing mitigation - enable canary fallback to smaller model variant (13b->7b) on region if p95 > 300ms (manual trigger until rollout policy updated).

Action items (owners + rough ETA):
- Marco: bisect PR 1423 to the exact commit introducing the perf regression; create microbench PR to capture failing case (ETA: 48h).
- Sofia: roll back greedy timeout in batcher on the canary pool and run the full nightly benchmark suite (ETA: 24h). Linked INF-3150.
- Diego: smoke tests with cudnn previous version across two pool configs and report delta (ETA: 24–36h).
- Priya: draft short customer note and pre-approved mitigation scripts for on-call to trigger fallback (ETA: 8h).
- Asha: coordinate dashboard alerts thresholds and add synthetic test targeted at 2–4k tokens (ETA: 12h).

Open questions / risks:
- If both kernel change and cudnn upgrade contribute, we need a layered mitigation (rollback or tune kernels + image pin).
- Rolling back PR 1423 has code ownership and test coverage implications — will need a temporary hotfix branch and announcements to owners.
- Canary rollback vs progressive mitigation tradeoffs: some customers prefer no regressions even during short rollback windows.

Temporary mitigations applied during meeting:
- Canary in us-west-2 rolled back to previous model-serve image (gradual) — monitoring enabled.
- Enabled fallback route in the routing policy to prefer 7b variant for affected customer orgs in region us-west-2.

Follow-ups scheduled:
- Deep-dive session Monday 2024-12-16 10:00 PT (agenda: kernel microbenching, batcher telemetry, driver image reconciliation). Invites: eng-serving-runtime, infra, applied-ml.
- Postmortem doc to be created once root cause established; assign author after Monday session.

Quick logs / reproducible commands used during triage (copy/paste):
- run bench: ./scripts/run_bench.sh --model openchat-13b-8k --pool canary-usw2 --batch-config batcher-v2.json --duration 600 --log-level debug --tag triage-dec12
- trace collection: ./tools/trace_collect --run-id nightly-bench-2024-12-11-03 --out /tmp/traces.tgz
- kernel microbench: python3 infra/tools/kernel_microbench.py --kernel attention_v2 --seq-len 2048 --heads 32 --batch 4

Raw snippet from grafana trace (redacted):
  - attention_v2::apply_gemm  
    - avg 120ms -> 210ms (regression case)
    - observed increased memcpy at offsets for kv-cache (approx +48ms)

If you make progress on any of the action items, paste short updates below and I'll fold into next sync notes.

Notes-to-self / loose thoughts (informal):
- consider adding targeted unit which runs long-seq padded shapes to CI; catches kernel-batching interactions earlier.
- investigate a small-heap local allocator to reduce memcpy overhead on KV cache.

End of notes.
